sales.title: PONTIC KINGDOM. Mithradates IV (169-150 BC or 150-120 BC). AR tetradrachm (35mm, 16.98 gm, 12h). NGC Choice AU 5/5 - 2/5, Fine Style, brushed.  Diademed and bearded head of Mithradates IV right, diadem ties falling behind / ΒΑΣΙΛΕΩΣ / ΜΙΘΡΑΔΑΤΟΥ / ΦΙΛΟΠΑΤΟΡΟΣ / ΚΑΙ ΦΙΛΑΔΕΛΦΟΥ Perseus standing facing, nude save for cloak over shoulders, with pointed cap and winged shoes, head of Medusa in outstretched right hand, harpa cradled in left arm; eight-pointed star over upwards crescent above. SNG von Aulock 6674 var. (no monogram). HGC 7, 326. Only one other example of this type in sales archives. High reliefs and intricate details on this extremely rare type; certainly one of the finest examples.   Perseus appears on this reverse to highlight him as an ancestor of the Persians. The Persian King Xerxes I (486-465 BC) was aware of the etymology at the time of his invasion of mainland Greece in 480 BC and used it to convince the Argives to capitulate. The link between Perseus and the Persians was deeply entrenched by 2nd century BC and Mithradates IV, who was of Iranian descent, used it to associate the Pontic Mithradatic dynasty with the greatness of the Persic Achaemenid Empire. The irony of having a Greek hero to propagate a connection to an Iranian empire that was frequently in conflict with the states of Greece would be further cemented by the conscious Hellenizing of Mithradates IV's portrait.
